transcript:
Header: Crescent AI activation intake sync
Date: 2026-03-24 14:00 PT
Duration: 63 minutes
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sophie Grant (Redwood CSM); Evan Rhodes (CTO), Priya Desai (Lead ML Eng), Luis Moreno (Infra), Zoe Park (Product)

Summary block (auto): quick notes recorded by recorder - pilot scope, security reqs, and next steps.

00:00 Nina Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Nina from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with Marcus our SE and Sophie our CSM. can we do quick intros?
00:18 Evan Rhodes: Evan here, CTO at Crescent AI, we build retrieval augmented agents for enterprise and we're looking to put some of our inference on a managed stack, but with control over data.
00:28 Priya Desai: Priya lead ML eng, i'll own the prompt sets and evaluation.
00:34 Luis Moreno: Luis, infra, i'll handle networking and secrets.
00:39 Zoe Park: Zoe, product, here to track timeline and success metrics.
00:45 Marcus Li: Marcus, SE at Redwood, i'll run the perf baselines and help with the VPC peering details.
00:51 Sophie Grant: Sophie, CSM - i'll coordinate the pilot runbook and onboarding ops.

01:05 Nina Patel: Great. high level objectives - quick alignment: pilot to validate latency & cost for 2 production prompt flows, prove private data handling with our VPC option, and then decide between Dedicated or Private for Q3. is that fair?
01:22 Evan Rhodes: Yes, that sounds right, timeline we have is internal buy-in by mid April so we need the pilot results in the first two weeks of April ideally.
01:31 Priya Desai: just to add we have two workloads: a short chat flow (avg 120 tokens) and a document Q/A flow (avg 600 tokens). throughput target is about 200 r/s during peak, but we'll start smaller.
01:44 Marcus Li: ok good. for that mix we usually recommend looking at small-batch policies and prefix cache. quick question: are you planning to send RAG embeddings through Redwood or host embeddings elsewhere?
01:55 Priya Desai: embeddings will live in-house right now, we'll just call the generator for final answer; no embedding calls to Redwood.
02:03 Marcus Li: got it. that simplifies billing and we can focus on token generation costs.

02:20 Sophie Grant: on the security side, Crescent mentioned strong compliance needs - can you outline the must-haves?
02:26 Evan Rhodes: yes, must have SOC2 or SOC2-in-progress, SAML SSO, audit logs retained 12 months, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. also data residency in us-east required.
02:39 Nina Patel: Redwood supports SSO + SAML, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations in our Private deployments; for Hosted we can do encrypted-in-transit and separate retention policies but KMS customer keys only in Private.
02:53 Priya Desai: can you clarify differences between Dedicated and Private, sometimes we're not sure which is the right fit.
03:00 Marcus Li: sure - Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation and commitments; you get performance SLOs and predictable throughput but keys are managed by Redwood. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you customer-managed KMS, VPC peering or private link into your cloud, and full control of keys and network egress. If KMS is showstopper, Private is the choice.
03:21 Luis Moreno: we need customer KMS, so it sounds like Private is required, at least for production. pilot could run in Hosted if we can route traffic via a peered VPC?
03:32 Marcus Li: we do have a Private control-plane option where the runtime sits in your VPC or peered network. for pilot we can do a scoped Private pilot in your staging account, or a Hosted pilot with strict retention and NDAs; both are possible.

03:50 Nina Patel: Sophie, for the pilot runbook can we agree on scope: 1 month pilot, focus on two prompt flows; Redwood will run perf baseline and provide cost per 1k tokens estimates; Crescent provides prompt corpus and access to staging environment.
04:04 Sophie Grant: yes i'll draft that and share the onboarding runbook link.

04:20 Zoe Park: what are the success criteria from Redwood's POV and what should we expect to see in the final report?
04:27 Nina Patel: we will measure median p95 latency under expected concurrency, token cost breakdown, error rates, and a quality check — we'll compare a small eval of your golden prompts to ensure no regression. also recommendations on batching and quantization if appropriate.
04:43 Priya Desai: when you say quantization recommendations, do you run that on model variants or is that something we need to test locally?
04:50 Marcus Li: we'll recommend quantized variants compatible with our runtime and provide a cost/quality tradeoff table. we can also run a quantized baseline during the pilot if you allow the model artifacts in staging. sometimes model name mappings get a little fuzzed in transcripts, e.g., we'll refer to model variants like rdx-large-8q but i'll make sure to give exact names in the doc.
05:12 Evan Rhodes: ok good. about networking - Luis, any constraints?
05:17 Luis Moreno: we have strict egress controls, need VPC peering or private link and IP allowlist. also need to ensure the KMS key policy allows Redwood's service principal for envelope encryption.
05:29 Marcus Li: noted. for peering we typically need an account ID and CIDR ranges; i'll send our peering template after the call.
05:36 Nina Patel: can you also confirm whether you'll provide a staging env with sample traffic generator or do you want Redwood to run a synthetic load?
05:45 Luis Moreno: we can provide a basic traffic generator and staging cluster but it will take us a few days to provision access.
05:53 Marcus Li: that's fine, Redwood can run an initial synthetic baseline in our test harness and then we'll re-run once we have staging access to validate.
06:05 Sophie Grant: i'll coordinate access details. i'll also add the SSO and KMS checklist to the runbook.

06:18 Zoe Park: curious about observability - what telemetry do you surface?
06:23 Marcus Li: token-level cost, per-route latency percentiles, error traces, request-level metadata; plus we can add tracing hooks to your APM. there may be slight name mangling from auto transcribe, sometimes it writes KV cache as 'kay-vee cache' in notes.
06:40 Priya Desai: ha, noted. for evaluation we'll want both latency and semantic quality; can Redwood store eval traces for the duration of pilot?
06:48 Nina Patel: yes we can store evaluation artifacts in your tenancy for Private, or in Hosted with export options. retention settings configurable.

07:00 Evan Rhodes: question on pricing - what does pilot cost look like and do you have committed options?
07:07 Nina Patel: we have a pilot credit for small customers, otherwise pilot pricing depends on runtime mode. we'll send three options: Hosted trial (low friction), Dedicated reserved (predictable throughput), Private scoped pilot (higher setup but meets KMS needs). i'll include committed discount tiers and per-token cost examples in the deck.
07:27 Zoe Park: can you also include estimated engineering time to production?
07:31 Sophie Grant: yes typical onboarding is 4-6 weeks to production depending on network and compliance work; pilot to PO conversion usually 6-8 weeks once pilot results are accepted.

07:45 Marcus Li: ok timeline: this week - share runbook + templates; by 2026-03-30 customer to share prompts and dev access; 2026-04-01 we run initial baseline; week of 2026-04-06 we deep-dive on security and finalize recommendations.
07:58 Evan Rhodes: sounds reasonable.

08:10 Priya Desai: small nit - do you have any restrictions on prompt data that might include PII? we have some masked PII but some flows will include user names.
08:20 Nina Patel: with Private and customer KMS, data can remain encrypted and you control key rotation; we also offer redaction and tokenization helpers in the runbook. for Hosted we can discuss contractual DPA terms and suppression.

08:41 Luis Moreno: about audit logs - format and retention?
08:45 Marcus Li: logs are JSON lines with request id, timestamp, model, tokens in/out, latency, and optional user metadata. retention configurable; default Hosted is 90 days, we can extend to 12 months on enterprise plans.

09:03 Zoe Park: any caveats on model rollouts / canary?
09:07 Marcus Li: yes you can pin a model version, roll out with traffic weight, and configure automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant on errors. our console shows per-model dashboards so you can track regressions.

09:20 Sophie Grant: we'll also provide a success checklist: 1) prompts uploaded 2) staging access granted 3) perf run results 4) security checklist satisfied 5) pilot review meeting.
09:31 Nina Patel: perfect. any other questions from Crescent?
09:33 Priya Desai: nothing else right now.

09:40 Evan Rhodes: one last ask - can Redwood provide a short checklist for procurement? procurement will want SOC2 attestation and sample contract language for data handling.
09:50 Nina Patel: yes we'll include SOC2 report, sample SLA language, and a procurement brief in the Materials pack.

10:00 Marcus Li: i'll follow up with peering template and perf template, Sophie will share the runbook and Nina will send pricing and pilot agreement.

10:12 Sophie Grant: i'll also set the next meeting - tech deep-dive - target week of 2026-03-30.

10:20 Nina Patel: thanks everyone. recap: we do pilot, Crescent shares prompts and staging access, Redwood runs baseline, security deep-dive scheduled. we'll circulate notes and action items after.

10:35 Evan Rhodes: thanks all.

-- End of recording --

Notes: Auto-transcription had a few mis-typed product names (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated' - minor). References to external docs provided above.
